need-to-know.answer: The main activity core and restrooms operate seasonally. Kent County says 2026 season-pass sales have ended and had not posted final beach closing dates when checked; day tickets remain listed, but weather, staffing, water conditions, or an updated closing notice can shorten access. Verify the beach page before leaving.

launch-mi-grand-rapids-riverside-park.sourceLabel: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation

restroom.answer: Restrooms serve developed areas seasonally. The City's event guidance says all park restrooms are winterized and closed from October through May; individual buildings can also close for maintenance, flooding, or daily service limits. Confirm current status before a restroom-dependent visit.

splash-pad.answer: Riverside Park is not a swimming or splash-pad destination. Its managed water recreation is the 2026 seasonal kayak rental at the accessible lagoon launch: Fridays 4:00-8:00 p.m. and Saturdays and Sundays 10:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. through the planned August 30 final date, weather permitting. Rentals cost $5 per hour for ages 17 and under and $10 per hour for adults, include boats and lifejackets, and are first come, first rented. Check the closure hotline before traveling.
splash-pad.sourceLabel: City of Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation

need-to-know.answer: Low riverfront paths, launches, ponds, and parking areas can flood after high water or heavy rain. Kayak rentals and park programs post cancellations through the City closure hotline at 616-456-3699. Obey barricades and check current event, flood, and rental conditions before relying on a particular entrance.
